reviews.title: I’m actually sad
reviews.text: I’ve been a subscriber for a long time and really enjoyed tracking my reading and knowing how much I’ve read throughout the years but the app continues to get worse and unfortunately I can’t continue to pay for something that is no longer meeting my expectations.

reviews.title: You have to Pay to Use
reviews.text: They let you get all the way through to logging onto Amazon or Goodreads then tell you it will cost you to go further. Scam!

reviews.title: Not functioning properly
reviews.text:
I’m a lifetime subscriber who has seen the app degrade over time. Reading sessions don’t work. The app won’t track anything, and the sessions can’t be manually entered either. It is hit or miss which books it works for. 

The developer asks for feedback, says he’ll support the product, by multiple support tickets over the last year have gone ignored (except for the auto email that says he’ll get to you shortly!). 

I’m giving two stars for the idea. Sadly execution is not there. Don’t be like me. Use the free version. Or better yet, find an app that works as promised.

reviews.title: Very disappointed
reviews.text: Take my info before letting me know how much it costs. And then no way to delete my information. Pretty scammy

reviews.title: Subscription Based
reviews.text: A great app, but the fact that a subscription is required for most things and you can’t even record every time you read is a let down.

reviews.title: Not good

reviews.title: Update deleted everything!
reviews.text: This had been a wonderful app to track reading progress etc. I specifically used it to manage a large list of "to read" books. I updated the app and presto five years of reading, notes & information gone. No books listed. No data. Well done bookshelf. Terrible app

reviews.title: Good, not great
reviews.text:
This app is closer to what I want in a reading log: I can log both physical and audio books easily; I can save quotes if I want to; the app can make recommendations on what to read next; I can easily scan and keep lists of my current books. 

Where it falls short is the stats feature. It’s counting my audiobooks as “pages read” rather than “hours listened.” It also doesn’t separate out audiobooks from physical books in the “books read” area. Other apps will separate them out in a pie graph. But this app only uses bar charts and there aren’t really any great analytics coming out of it. 

The app developers also force a reading goal for users. I don’t have a goal. I just want to track what I read. Plain and simple. By forcing me into a goal tracking system, it makes me feel like I’m not meeting some promise that I made to myself (which I didn’t, the app literally won’t let me bypass this). Thinking long term, I wouldn’t want to use this to track anything. I would constantly feel like I’m failing.

reviews.title: Terrible no value app

reviews.title: Reading list is just gone??
reviews.text: My app was glitching and nothing would show up when i searched booked titles so i checked if there was an update. After updating the app ALL the books i had on my “to read” list are gone. Super disappointing because this was my go to app when I was at the bookstore and couldn’t remember book reccs I saw and wanted to read. Will probably end up deleting the app and just note my To Reads in my notes app…..

reviews.title: Bad, misleading AI design
reviews.text:
I tested the AI chat with The British Are Coming by Rick Atkinson. The chat box said I could request chapter by chapter summaries, so I asked if the book discusses the debate around the Declaration of Independence in Philadelphia up through chapter 14. The AI chat said yes, that the book covers the Declaration debate in Philadelphia and discusses Thomas Jefferson and John Adams.

The problem here is that not a single chapter has been set in Philadelphia so far, Jefferson and Adams are barely mentioned, and the book is mostly about key battles, not the debates around the Declaration.

The AI chat should express its limitations when it is asked a question it doesn’t know the answer to. Plenty of current models do that, they don’t guess incorrect information. And marketing for this app should reflect that limitation instead of offering chapter summaries.

I like the design of this app more than any other book app out there right now, but I can’t justify paying a subscription for misleading marketing and an AI chat that didn’t know its own limitations.

reviews.title: Good, but often buggy
reviews.text:
I’ve reviewed a LOT of reading apps trying to find the best one, and I think this is it. It would get 5 stars but it’s pretty buggy — select a book from your reading list maybe it will open, maybe it won’t. End a reading session, the UI might be overlapping making it exceptionally hard to select a page number, or maybe it’ll work great. iCloud syncing has never been reliable for me.

The app does get updates, and the updates do fix bugs, until the come back, or new ones are added.

reviews.title: Buggy!
reviews.text: Really loved this app! Began cataloging my whole library collection until recently! Bugs bugs bugs! Book covers are blurred then when you fix them they never save and go black! Even when opening on another device! Reading timer doesn’t work anymore and it’s gone from my favourite app to one I’m struggling not to delete!

reviews.title: Canceled subscription still charged
reviews.text: I didn’t realize there would be a subscription so I did the free trial and canceled it before the trial even ended. 4 days after it “ended” money was taken from my account at 2AM. I thought someone hacked my card. Do not recommend

reviews.title: The most complex book tracking app…
reviews.text: This is an app I was excited to download and use. However, I never really go to use it. So much is hidden behind the pay wall. It’s great if you remember to constantly open the app and put it in reading mode. If you do not they make is so convoluted just to manually log in your reading time. Everything is based off % of book finished and not pages. So sitting here trying to manually calculate how much more I read from the last 6% I read is just stupid. Mind you this is supposed to be an app to track my reading. They manage to make this way more difficult and expensive. I never go to track my reading so I moved to Fable. They fixed something that was never broken and said how can we make this extra and costly. I deleted it.

reviews.title: Unusable
reviews.text: It pains me to write this review as someone who has used this app for the last four years, it really does hurt to see it essentially become unusable when I tried to either start the reading timer or I tried to add a previous reading session or even adding a new title to my library the app freezes and if I’m lucky on the 10th time, I’m able to actually complete what I set out to do. I have canceled my paid membership and at the end of the year I’m going to stop using this app I hope that in the future, the developers do listen to their customer base and communicate whether or not the app is getting a much-needed overhaul.

reviews.title: This was such a good app
reviews.text: I have ADHD and struggle to track my reading but I’m such a perfectionist that a terrible glitch in the calendar has ruined this app for me, it says that it is the correct date but the day of the week is one day behind and has been since September. This app is now unusable in my eyes because of it. The glitches on this app are so bad now it feels importable.
